name: Chau Doc fermented fish
summary: Mắm Châu Đốc is fish pickled with palm sugar, salt, chili, and garlic, stacked in the open at the market. It starts sweet and finishes salty, and you eat it with rice or carry a jar home.
origin: Châu Đốc, where mắm-making is a traditional trade. The workshops cluster at Núi Sam and the old Châu Phú A, and the town is called the kingdom of pickled fish.
culture: Mắm Châu Đốc carries two collective trademarks: đặc sản mắm Châu Đốc and đặc sản mắm thái Châu Đốc. The mắm lanes are busiest from December through July, when pilgrims come to Núi Sam.
taste: VnExpress on 2 Oct 2019 says Châu Đốc mắm leans sweet and finishes salty, which is why it goes so well with plain rice.
howToEat: Walk the stacks and taste before you buy. Eat it with rice on the spot, or take it home.

The An Giang portal lists mắm cá lóc, cá linh, cá trèn, cá sặc, and mắm thái. VnExpress on 2 Oct 2019 adds ba khía. The 26 Apr 2024 handbook names cá trèn, cá lóc, cá linh, and cá sọc. Cá sặc and cá sọc are both printed, so both stay.
Each stall posts its own prices.
Mắm cá mè vinh belongs to Tân Châu, not Châu Đốc.
where: Chợ Châu Đốc, and the stalls at the foot of Núi Sam.
